Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
question.worked_solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196632/assets/6e070d26915bcb11118f5a23f36b80038d5dd865e32a8517a12c10939ca02f0b.png)

First, we find the area of $△ABD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 8\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{85}^{∘} \\  & =24\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{85}^{∘} \\  & ≈23.908\,7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area of $△BCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BCD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 14\cdot 16\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{36.4}^{∘} \\  & =112\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{36.4}^{∘} \\  & ≈66.462\,9,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BCD} \\  & ≈23.908\,7+66.462\,9 \\  & ≈90.371\,6.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest integer, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $90.$
